identity.player: A boy or girl from a far-away, richer land who comes to seek knowledge; dressed differently; does not speak the language

city.name: Ilmara
city.meaning: say it IL-mah-rah · made up, from ‘ilm (“knowledge”)

centre.name: Centre
centre.line: The great masjid, the house of learning and the governor’s palace. The heart of the city.

east.name: East · River Market
east.line: Docks, traders and the inn. You land here and take a room on the edge of the market, inside the walls.

north.name: North
north.line: Gardens, orchards and the caravanserai where travellers rest.

west.name: West
west.line: Craftspeople: paper makers, bookbinders and potters.

south.name: South
south.line: Homes, wells, and the animal market where farmers bring their goods.

city.map_title_line: Walls, four gates, five parts. Tap a part.

world.title: The open field
world.line: {n} small towns without walls · main and side quests
world.towns_note: Placeholder names and positions on a 400 x 225 map; real towns are designed later
world.town_toast: {town}: a small town for main and side quests (designed later).

inn.name: Inn
inn.line: Your room by the quay. Bread included.

masjid.name: Masjid
masjid.line: The adhan is called from its roof five times a day.

arrival.kicker: Arrival · River Market quay · Rich in the wrong coins

beats.text: Dawn. The boat bumps against the River Market quay. You carry a travel bag, a book from home and a heavy purse of foreign silver. The crowd shouts in words you do not know.

choices.label: Step off into the crowd
choices.reply: Porters, sacks, goats. Nobody looks at you twice - except at your clothes.

choices.label: Wait until the crowd thins
choices.reply: The quay quietens. A boy points you towards two money-changers.

beats.text: A trader holds up your silver coin and shakes his head. Two money-changers sit by the quay. One works slowly at a scale everyone can watch. The other waves you over eagerly with a wide smile.

choices.label: Go to the one with the open scale
choices.reply: He weighs every coin in front of you and counts twenty local coins into your hand.

choices.label: Go to the smiling one
choices.reply: He counts fast and presses coins into your hand. Twelve. You cannot tell if that is right.

beats.text: At the inn by the quay, the innkeeper holds up two fingers, points at a room, then at the bread on the table.

choices.label: Pay for one night
choices.reply: A small room with a window over the water. It is yours.

beats.text: At sunset a voice rises over the rooftops from the masjid nearby. People stop what they are doing and walk towards it.

choices.label: Follow them
choices.reply: Inside, an old man with dates in his pocket notices you.

arrival.end_fair: Your silver was changed fairly. At two coins a night it will last you about ten days.
arrival.end_cheated: Something about the smiling changer bothers you. Later, at the market scales, you may find out you were cheated.
arrival.cheat_found_after_lesson: Now you can read a scale - and you realise the smiling money-changer gave you 12 coins for silver worth 20.
arrival.effect_time_note: effect.time = minutes after midnight the clock jumps to (1095 = 18:15, Maghrib)

inn.paid: You sleep in your paid room ({n} nights left). Morning comes.
inn.coins: You pay {n} coins and sleep. Morning comes.
inn.broom: You cannot pay, so you sweep the stable for a straw bed. Morning comes.

clock.congregation_rule: At the masjid from the adhan until 5 minutes after the iqamah
clock.missed_rule: A prayer not prayed before its time ends is missed; a prayer whose time ended before the game started is not counted
clock.duration_format: "{h} h {m} min", or "{m} min" under an hour
clock.pray_friday: Pray Friday prayer with the congregation
clock.masjid_after_prayed: You have prayed {prayer}. The masjid is quiet.

record.title: Your prayers
record.note: Only you see this. Prayer gives no coins and no trust.

clock.real_reminder: parked - not in this LOCK (Founder: "No no no setting no nothing")

teacher.name: Idris, the imam
teacher.who: The masjid’s imam: warm, fatherly, a little slow on his feet, always with dates in his pocket.
teacher.how: Teaches through sharing and stories, told with his hands while you learn the words.

beats.text: After Maghrib the imam sees you sitting alone. He sits beside you, opens a cloth of dates and says softly: {bismillah}

choices.label: Repeat it and take a date
choices.reply: He nods, pleased, and takes one too.

choices.label: Take a date
choices.reply: He smiles and says the word again as you eat.

beats.text: He pours you water from a clay jug.

choices.label: Say thank you in your language
choices.reply: He tilts his head, then teaches you his way of saying it.

choices.label: Bow your head
choices.reply: He pats your shoulder and teaches you the word anyway.

beats.text: He says it slowly so you can copy him: {shukran}

choices.label: Copy him
choices.reply: “Shukran,” you say. He laughs - your accent is terrible, and he loves it.

beats.text: With his hands he tells a story: a traveller, a long road, a light at the end. Then he points to the floor: {laylan}

choices.label: Nod
choices.reply: After Isha. He wants to tell you more stories.

teacher.end: New: come back to the imam after Isha for a story.
teacher.kicker: The masjid, River Market · {when} · words you know: {n}

language.rule: A word the traveller has not learned shows in the town's language, in a different colour; once learned it shows in English with the town word after it in brackets
